subject: Law Department Staffing Reductions for School Funding
overview: The City Council held its sixth preliminary budget hearing for Fiscal Year 2025, reviewing several municipal departments. The meeting was headlined by a contentious proposal to eliminate an in-house legal position and significant presentations on municipal infrastructure and technology upgrades.

items.title: Fire Department Budget Review
items.summary: Chief Todd Evans discussed a 4% budget increase driven by fixed contract costs, current staffing shortages of 17 members, and a federal SAFER grant application to hire 11 new firefighters.

items.title: Parking Department Budget Review
items.summary: Director Faye Morrison reported that the department has collected nearly $2 million in outstanding ticket revenue and is transitioning to a self-sustaining model utilizing new permitting software and hardware.

items.title: DPW Cemetery Division
items.summary: Commissioner Tim McGivern highlighted an $8 million estimate for historic building preservation and ongoing soil removal projects at the cemetery.

items.title: DPW Engineering Division
items.summary: City Engineer Owen Wartella outlined plans for water infrastructure replacement and flood mitigation projects while noting that the department is currently at maximum staffing capacity.

items.title: DPW Forestry Division
items.summary: The division is awaiting results from a tree inventory and a vulnerability assessment to develop a long-term urban forestry master plan.

items.title: DPW Highway Division
items.summary: The budget reflects a 10% increase primarily due to three new waste management contracts for trash, recycling, and composting.

items.title: DPW Parks Division
items.summary: The council reviewed routine fixed cost increases for field maintenance and the upkeep of the city's 15 athletic fields.

items.title: DPW Water and Sewer Enterprise Fund
items.summary: Commissioner McGivern detailed a 35-year plan for pipe replacement and noted that the majority of the budget increase is driven by MWRA assessments.

items.title: Debt Service and Bonds
items.summary: Director Bob Dickinson reviewed an $800,000 combined increase in debt service for the General Fund and Water/Sewer Fund due to principal and interest payments.

items.title: Electrical Department
items.summary: Superintendent Steve Randazzo discussed ongoing efforts to upgrade streetlights to LED and bring pedestrian crossings into ADA compliance.

items.title: Elections Department
items.summary: New Elections Manager Danielle Petrantonio was introduced, and officials discussed state reimbursements for early voting costs and the upcoming federal election cycle.

items.title: Facilities Department
items.summary: Director Paul Riggi reported on HVAC maintenance contracts, the reopening of Engine 3, and a new 'house doctor' program for architectural services.

items.title: Information Technology
items.summary: Director Rich Lane presented a digital transformation plan including the installation of a municipal fiber optic network and a replacement of the city's legacy phone system.

items.title: Law Department
items.summary: The administration proposed eliminating the Assistant City Solicitor position to redirect funds to the school department, a move that met significant opposition from several councilors.
